This is Peter Lynch’s favorite metric and I like it too because it ties valuation to growth and I prefer using a 2026 to 2028 window so the multiple adjusts for how fast the business is actually compounding.

For example $AMD trades at ~47x forward earnings but earnings are expected to grow from $5.71 in 2026 to $20.29 in 2028 implying a ~89% earnings CAGR and PEG of ~0.5x.

posts.name: Shay Boloor
posts.text:
Pretty wild that GPUs are now the only balanced part of the AI supply chain while DRAM, SSDs, hard drives and chip substrates face lead times 2–5x longer than normal.

That means even if $AMZN, $MSFT, $GOOGL and $META secure their $NVDA GPUs, they still need CPUs, memory and packaging materials like ABF that can take nearly a year to source versus just three months normally.

That's a massive opportunity for $MU and $SKHY in DRAM and HBM, $SNDK in enterprise SSDs, $WDC and $STX in hard drives and $INTC and $AMD in CPUs as AI agents drive demand across entire infrastructure stack.

posts.name: Shay Boloor
posts.text:
Morgan Stanley sees ~160 GW of U.S. data center power demand through 2029 against an insane ~77 GW shortfall leaving nearly half of that demand at risk of going unpowered.

That’s a massive opportunity for $GEV with its sold-out gas turbines and $BE with onsite fuel cells that can generate electricity without relying on turbines.

And getting that power into AI data centers creates another opportunity for $VRT in power delivery and cooling, $FPS in transformers and prefabricated electrical systems and $ON and $NVTS in improving efficiency through SiC and GaN.

posts.text:
Crypto exchange volume dropped about 30% after the 10/10 crash

Bitget CEO Gracy Chen on where trading activity is moving, and why smaller exchanges were hit even harder

"Right after 10/10, we see a volume decrease of maybe 30% on average among all the top exchanges. For the smaller exchanges it could be even worse because there's like the Matthew effect."

"The big ones will become bigger, and the smaller ones will just shrink and become smaller and eventually die down. And that's indeed the situation that we've seen."

"What's quite interesting now that we are observing is a lot of users come to our platform to trade non-crypto assets. At its peak earlier this year, non-crypto assets counted for almost 40% of our total trading volume."

"One is tokenized commodities or commodity perpetuals, and the other one is stocks in general, especially US stocks."

posts.text:
Of the $388M stolen from Bitget, only $1-2M has been frozen so far

Bitget CEO Gracy Chen says crypto still struggles to trace stolen funds, while hackers shift from targeting keys to credentials

"They are more targeting credentials, processes, and trusted tools, rather than maybe originally mainly about private keys. Now we've done pretty good guarding of private keys, cold wallets, etc."

"But no exchange can address this alone. As an industry, we need to share intelligence around threats. We need to have a lot of fast coordination, especially when we are tracing illicit funds."

"On day one, you need to build your exchange with the mindset that they will be targeting you, especially if you grow bigger and have a lot of users and custodian funds."
